examples.source: Nora and Eli found a basket of apples after their walk. They were both hungry, and the basket was too heavy to carry far.
examples.cooperative_story: Nora and Eli found a basket of apples after their walk. They were both hungry, and the basket was too heavy to carry far. Nora suggested they share the apples and take turns carrying the basket. Eli agreed. They ate enough to feel better and carried the rest home together.
examples.non_cooperative_story: Nora and Eli found a basket of apples after their walk. They were both hungry, and the basket was too heavy to carry far. While Eli looked for a path, Nora filled her bag with the best apples and took the light basket. She reached home with plenty to eat before the rain began.

metadata.changed_social_choice: Nora takes the shared apples for herself
metadata.causal_outcome: she carries away the food and reaches home before the rain

examples.topic: mutual assistance versus successful independent defection
examples.source: Sam and Bea had one wagon for their toys. They planned to take turns pulling it up the hill, but Sam wanted to get to the picnic first.
examples.cooperative_story: Sam and Bea had one wagon for their toys. They planned to take turns pulling it up the hill, but Sam wanted to get to the picnic first. Sam pulled while Bea pushed, and then they switched. Working together, they got the wagon to the top quickly and reached the picnic with their toys.
examples.non_cooperative_story: Sam and Bea had one wagon for their toys. They planned to take turns pulling it up the hill, but Sam wanted to get to the picnic first. When Bea paused to tie her shoe, Sam pulled the wagon the rest of the way alone. He reached the picnic first and chose a shady place for himself.

metadata.changed_social_choice: Sam stops following the agreed turn-taking plan
metadata.causal_outcome: he reaches the picnic first and chooses the shady place

examples.source: Lina wanted to paint a picture, and Max had the only blue paint. Max needed a clean brush for his own picture.
examples.cooperative_story: Lina wanted to paint a picture, and Max had the only blue paint. Max needed a clean brush for his own picture. Lina offered to wash the brush when they finished, so Max shared the blue paint first. They both finished their pictures, and Max had a clean brush ready for his next one.
examples.non_cooperative_story: Lina wanted to paint a picture, and Max had the only blue paint. Max needed a clean brush for his own picture. Max kept the blue paint for his own work and started before Lina could ask again. He finished his picture in time to hang it in the school display.

metadata.changed_social_choice: Max withholds the scarce blue paint
metadata.causal_outcome: he completes his picture in time for the display

examples.source: Ava and Ben both wanted the last kite for the windy afternoon. The kite was caught in a low tree branch, and the clouds were moving closer.
examples.cooperative_story: Ava and Ben both wanted the last kite for the windy afternoon. The kite was caught in a low tree branch, and the clouds were moving closer. Ava held the ladder while Ben reached the kite, then they agreed to take turns flying it. They got the kite down safely and both enjoyed it before the rain.
examples.non_cooperative_story: Ava and Ben both wanted the last kite for the windy afternoon. The kite was caught in a low tree branch, and the clouds were moving closer. Ava climbed the low branch while Ben searched for a ladder. She freed the kite and began flying it in the open field before the rain arrived.

metadata.changed_social_choice: Ava takes the kite without agreeing to share it
metadata.causal_outcome: she flies the kite before the rain

examples.topic: rivalry with fair competition distinct from exploitation
examples.source: Milo and Pip entered the garden race. They each had a small watering can and wanted their row of flowers to bloom first.
examples.cooperative_story: Milo and Pip entered the garden race. They each had a small watering can and wanted their row of flowers to bloom first. Milo watered his row carefully and helped Pip fix a bent marker. His flowers opened in the sun, and his row won the garden ribbon.
examples.non_cooperative_story: Milo and Pip entered the garden race. They each had a small watering can and wanted their row of flowers to bloom first. Milo followed the race rules, watered his own row on schedule, and chose a sunny spot for the pots. His flowers opened first, and his row won the garden ribbon.

metadata.changed_social_choice: Milo competes by tending only his own row within the rules
metadata.causal_outcome: his row blooms first and wins the ribbon
